title: FreeBSD support?
body:
### What platform is your computer?

FreeBSD

### How did you attempt to install or upgrade?

Tried to install bun on a https://www.nearlyfreespeech.net server, which I now realize is running FreeBSD. Unfortunately it looks like bun only supports Linux.

### What do you see instead?

ELF interpreter /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 not found, error 2 
Abort trap

### Additional information

_No response_

comments.author: participant11
comments.body:
so ... bun now works on FreeBSD 14.2-RELEASE amd64 & arm64 via [linuxlator](https://docs.freebsd.org/en/books/handbook/linuxemu/) but it was easier to get my notes off 15.0-CURRENT.

```
$ doas service linux onestart
$ doas pkg install -yr FreeBSD linux_base-rl9
$ cd /tmp
$ curl -#L https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.2.5/bun-linux-aarch64.zip -o - | tar xzf -
$ cd bun-linux-aarch64/
$ brandelf -t Linux *
$ chmod +x *
$ ./bun -h
Bun is a fast JavaScript runtime, package manager, bundler, and test runner. (1.2.5+013fdddc6)

Usage: bun <command> [...flags] [...args]

Commands:
  run       ./my-script.ts       Execute a file with Bun
            lint                 Run a package.json script
  test                           Run unit tests with Bun
  x         next                 Execute a package binary (CLI), installing if needed (bunx)
  repl                           Start a REPL session with Bun
  exec                           Run a shell script directly with Bun
...

$ uname -a
FreeBSD straylight 15.0-CURRENT FreeBSD 15.0-CURRENT main-n275676-deadb1668a17 GENERIC-NODEBUG arm64
$ freebsd-version -kru
15.0-CURRENT
```

I would expect much of bun to work out of the box, but if there are any issues please report these over at https://bugs.freebsd.org/ so we can track and fix them.

Hopefully the work on getting native FreeBSD bun.sh working will still happen, though,
this is already a great start.

comments.author: participant30
comments.body:
1. The shell script at https://bun.sh/install has not been updated to detect and work correctly with FreeBSD.
2. The [main README](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/README.md) has not had any additions to mention that FreeBSD is now an official platform, nor how to build for it.
3. edit: this last one was my fault, I should've read [the cpu requirements](https://bun.com/docs/installation#cpu-requirements)

> As far as I can tell, the x64 zipfiles in https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/tag/bun-v1.3.14 were not built with the correct architecture mappings; I get  `illegal hardware instruction` when trying to run the bun binary inside each of them on a standard x86_64 Intel Xeon CPU. 😕
